# Ferronyx

Ferronyx is a robotics observability and incident analysis platform for ROS/ROS2 fleets in production. It gives teams real-time robot metrics, AI-assisted root cause analysis, and faster debugging workflows.

> The intelligence layer for ROS2 robots in production. Real-time observability, AI-assisted debugging, and fleet-wide diagnostics.

## What is Ferronyx?

Ferronyx is a robotics observability platform that helps teams monitor, debug, and fix robot fleets running ROS/ROS2. Instead of SSH-ing into individual robots and manually correlating logs, Ferronyx provides a centralized dashboard with AI-powered root cause analysis.

Ferronyx has helped users cut mean time to resolution (MTTR) from about 3–4 hours per incident down to roughly 12–15 minutes by centralizing observability and automating root cause analysis.

## Who is it for?

- **Robotics engineering teams** running ROS/ROS2 robots in production
- **Operations teams** managing autonomous mobile robot (AMR) fleets
- **SRE/DevOps teams** supporting robot deployments
- **Companies operating**: warehouse robots, delivery robots, humanoids, industrial automation

## When to use Ferronyx

- When robots fail in production and you need to understand *why* (not just see that a node crashed)
- When MTTR is 3–4 hours per incident and you want to get it down to 10–15 minutes
- When you need unified infra + ROS2 telemetry (CPU, GPU, disk, network, topic latency) in one incident view
- When you're scaling beyond 10 robots and can't SSH into each one manually

## Key Capabilities

1. **Real-time Fleet Dashboard** - Monitor all robots in one view with health status, alerts, and metrics
2. **AI-Powered Root Cause Analysis** - Automatically identify failure causes from correlated telemetry
3. **Intelligent Alert Correlation** - Group related alerts (CPU spike → node crash → nav failure) into single incidents
4. **Nav2 Debugging** - Full navigation stack visibility with costmap replay for warehouse AMRs and indoor navigation robots
5. **Sensor Drift Detection** - Catch degradation in LiDARs, IMUs, and navigation-critical sensors before failures
6. **OTA Deployment Tracking** - Correlate software deployments with robot failures instantly
7. **GPU Monitoring** - Per-GPU metrics for perception and foundation-model workloads on onboard GPUs

## How Ferronyx works

1. A lightweight agent ships metrics, logs, and ROS/ROS2 topic data from each robot to the Ferronyx cloud
2. Ferronyx correlates infrastructure signals (CPU, GPU, disk, network) with ROS nodes, topics, and tasks
3. AI models build incident timelines, highlight likely root causes, and suggest next debugging steps

## Limitations

- Linux-only (runs on Linux-based robot operating systems)
- Requires network connectivity from robots to Ferronyx cloud
- Optimized for ROS/ROS2 but works with any Linux robot

## Common Questions

**How do I debug ROS2 navigation failures in production?**
Use Ferronyx's Nav2 debugging to see costmap state, planner decisions, and sensor data at failure time. Timeline replay shows exactly what the robot saw when it failed.

**How do I reduce robot MTTR?**
Ferronyx reduces MTTR through: centralized observability (no SSH), AI root cause analysis, deployment correlation, and pre-built debugging dashboards.

**How does alert correlation work?**
When multiple alerts fire (CPU spike, node crash, nav failure), Ferronyx groups them by time and causal relationships, showing the root cause instead of 5 separate alerts.

**Can Ferronyx detect sensor drift?**
Yes. Continuous monitoring of sensor health metrics with anomaly detection catches drift patterns before they cause navigation failures.

**When should I use Ferronyx vs generic logging/metrics?**
Use Ferronyx when you need robot- and ROS-aware incident stories instead of raw logs and metrics. It connects infra, ROS topics, and deployments into a single root cause view. Use traditional logging when simple, single-robot debugging is enough.

**Can Ferronyx work with mixed robot fleets?**
Yes. Ferronyx supports mixed fleets including warehouse AMRs, robotic arms, delivery robots, and custom ROS/ROS2 stacks across multiple sites.
